english.title: Master of ship contravene requirement relating to operating / loading conditions - merchant shipping
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the master of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), failed to ensure, when curves or tables of minimum operational metacentric height (GM) or maximum allowable KG versus draught were not provided, to ensure that the operating condition did not deviate from approved loading conditions, or verify by calculation that the stability requirements were satisfied for this loading condition
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 17(2)(a) and (3) of the Merchant Shipping (Cargo and Passenger Ship Construction and Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2023.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being the master of a ship
to which the Merchant Shipping (Cargo and Passenger Ship Construction and Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2023 applied
breached requirements relating to operating or loading conditions in paragraph 6 of regulation 5-1 of Chapter II-1 in the Annex to the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea 1974

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) See the defence available in regulation 17(4) of the Merchant Shipping (Cargo and Passenger Ship Construction and Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2023 for the person charged to prove that they took all reasonable steps to avoid the commission of the offence.(ii) This relates to regulations contained within Chapter II-1 of the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea 1974

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
